**SECTION 2: SCOPE OF INSPECTION**

This inspection was conducted in response to a complaint received on 2021-06-11 (Complaint Log No. C-2021-08812) regarding possible mold growth, water intrusion, and electrical hazards in common areas and individual dwelling units.

The inspection covered the following areas:

- Exterior building envelope (roof, siding, windows, foundation)
- Common hallways and stairwells
- Basement storage and mechanical rooms
- Laundry room (first floor)
- Five (5) dwelling units (Apt. 2B, Apt. 2D, Apt. 3A, Apt. 3C, Apt. 1C)
- Interior of two (2) vacant units (Apt. 3B and Apt. 1D)

**Units not inspected at the time of inspection:** Apt. 2A, Apt. 2C, Apt. 3D, Apt. 1A, Apt. 1B. Occupants not present; rescheduled for follow-up.

SDCI property records show Northgate Apartments address as 1205 NE 125th St, Seattle, WA 98125. Record status: current.

---

**SECTION 3: GENERAL OBSERVATIONS**

The following are general observations noted during the exterior and common-area walkthrough. Detailed findings, violation codes, and required remediation deadlines are listed in Section 4 (Findings and Violations).

1. **Exterior:** Siding generally in fair condition. Some areas of peeling paint noted on the west elevation near the ground-level utility room. Gutters on the north side of the building were partially clogged with leaves and debris. Downspout at the northeast corner was disconnected from the underground drain and discharging water directly against the foundation.

2. **Roof:** No visible signs of active leaking observed from the interior of the third-floor hallway. However, water staining was noted on the ceiling of the third-floor stairwell landing (see Finding No. 2).

3. **Windows:** Several windows in the common stairwells had condensation between the panes, indicating failed seals. Window hardware on the second-floor hallway window was missing the crank handle; window was in the closed position.

4. **Basement / Mechanical Room:** The basement hallway leading to the mechanical room had a musty odor. The floor drain near the water heater was dry. The water heater (mfg. 2015, serial no. W1508-3341) appeared to be in working order. No visible leaks at the time of inspection.

5. **Laundry Room:** Two (2) washing machines and two (2) dryers present. One dryer vent hose was disconnected at the wall connection, causing lint accumulation on the floor behind the dryer. No immediate fire hazard observed, but lint accumulation noted for housekeeping follow-up.

6. **Common Hallways:** Carpet in the second-floor hallway showed signs of water staining and discoloration in a 3-ft by 4-ft area near Apt. 2C. The carpet was dry at the time of inspection. A note was left for the building manager to check the area for possible leaks.

7. **Electrical Panel (Basement):** Main electrical panel was labeled and accessible. One (1) breaker was noted as not labeled (position 12). No signs of overheating or burnt wiring observed.

---
The building has one main entrance on the east side facing Rainier Ave S, with
secondary exits at the north and south ends of the building. Each floor has a
common hallway with a stairwell at both ends. The building has a single master
water meter and separate electrical meters for each unit, located in the basement.

The property manager, Marcus Delgado, has been in his position for approximately
eight (8) months. He reported that the previous property manager left without
providing complete maintenance records, and that some paperwork related to recent
repairs may be incomplete or missing. Mr. Delgado provided access to all common
areas and to three (3) units for inspection (Apt. 1B, Apt. 2C, and Apt. 3A).

---

SECTION 2: BUILDING SYSTEMS OVERVIEW

The following is a summary of building systems observed during the inspection.
Detailed findings and any violations are listed in Section 4 (Findings and
Violations).

2.1 Heating System: Each unit is equipped with an individual electric baseboard
heating system. The common hallways are heated by two (2) wall-mounted electric
heaters, one on the first floor and one on the third floor. Both heaters were
operational at the time of inspection. No gas lines are present in the building.

2.2 Hot Water System: One (1) 50-gallon electric water heater located in the
basement mechanical room. Manufacturer date 2015, serial no. W1508-3341. The unit
appeared to be in working order with no visible leaks at the time of inspection.
The temperature was not tested during this inspection.

2.3 Electrical System: Main electrical panel located in the basement mechanical
room. Panel was labeled and accessible. One (1) breaker was noted as not labeled
(position 12). No signs of overheating or burnt wiring observed. Each unit has a
separate sub-panel located in the unit's utility closet.

SDCI Inspection Report Form 12-B for Cedar Court Apartments records inspection_date as 2024-03-14. Record status: historical.

2.4 Plumbing System: The building has copper supply lines and cast iron waste
lines. No visible leaks observed in common areas. Water pressure was reported as
adequate by tenants interviewed during the inspection. The floor drain near the
water heater was dry at the time of inspection.

2.5 Fire Safety: Smoke detectors were observed in common hallways on all three
floors. A fire alarm panel is located in the first-floor hallway near the main
entrance. The panel showed no active alarms. Fire extinguishers were observed in
each common hallway, with the most recent inspection tag dated 2023-11. Two (2)
extinguishers were noted as having inspection tags that were difficult to read
due to wear, and this was noted for follow-up.

2.6 Ventilation: Bathroom exhaust fans were observed in the three (3) units
inspected. All fans were operational. The laundry room has a dedicated exhaust
system for the dryers. One (1) dryer vent hose was disconnected at the wall
connection in the laundry room, causing lint accumulation on the floor behind the
dryer. This was noted for housekeeping follow-up and does not constitute an
immediate fire hazard.

---

SECTION 3: UNITS INSPECTED

Three (3) units were inspected at the request of the property manager. Unit
interior inspections were limited to visual observation of the kitchen,
bathroom, and living areas. No destructive testing was performed. Tenants were
present in each unit during the inspection.

3.1 Unit 1B – Occupied by single tenant, leaseholder since 2022.
General condition: Fair. Kitchen counters showed signs of wear but were clean.
Bathroom had minor caulking gaps around the tub. No visible water damage or mold
observed. Window in the living room was operable. Tenant reported occasional
draft from the front door, which was noted for weather-stripping follow-up.

3.2 Unit 2C – Occupied by tenant Elena Ruiz, leaseholder since 2021.
General condition: Fair to good. Kitchen appeared clean and organized. Bathroom
was functional with no visible leaks. Tenant reported that the carpet in the
hallway outside her unit had been stained for several months and that she had
noticed a musty smell in the area. The carpet in the second-floor hallway near
Apt. 2C showed water staining and discoloration in a 3-ft by 4-ft area. The
carpet was dry at the time of inspection. A note was left for the building
manager to check the area for possible leaks. Tenant was cooperative and
provided access to all rooms.
3.4 Unit 3B – Occupied by tenant R. Chen, leaseholder since 2019.
General condition: Good. Kitchen and bathroom were clean and well maintained. No visible water damage, mold, or leaks observed. All windows operated properly. Tenant reported no complaints. Tenant stated she had not been contacted regarding any scheduled maintenance in the past six months and requested a copy of the building's pest control schedule.

---

SECTION 4: INSPECTION FINDING – BATHROOM CEILING, UNIT 3A

Finding: Mold in bathroom ceiling.

Location: Bathroom ceiling, directly above the tub, Unit 3A, Cedar Court Apartments.

Description: Visible dark spotting and discoloration on the ceiling surface, approximately 2 ft by 3 ft in area. The discoloration is consistent with mold growth. The ceiling surface was dry at the time of inspection. No active water source or leak was observed in the bathroom or in the unit above (Unit 4A was not inspected). The tenant reported the condition had been present for approximately three months and that she had notified the property management office in January 2024. The tenant also reported that the bathroom exhaust fan was noisy, which may have contributed to the condition.

Status: Pending further evaluation. No violation code or required completion date has been assigned at this time. The property manager was advised that a follow-up inspection will be scheduled to determine the extent of the condition and to verify that the tenant's report has been addressed. The property manager stated that a work order had been submitted to the maintenance contractor on 2024-03-11, but no documentation of the work order was available at the time of this inspection.

Photographs: Photographs 17 through 20 were taken of the bathroom ceiling condition in Unit 3A. Photograph 17 shows the overall bathroom ceiling. Photograph 18 is a close-up of the discolored area. Photographs 19 and 20 show the exhaust fan and the ceiling area adjacent to the fan. Photographs are attached to this report.

SECTION 5: COMMON AREA AND EXTERIOR NOTES (CONT.)

5.1 Exterior walkways and stairs: The concrete walkway at the north entrance had a crack approximately 1/4-inch wide running the length of the walkway. The crack was not lifting and did not present a trip hazard at the time of inspection. The handrail on the east stairway was loose at the top post and required tightening. This was noted for maintenance follow-up.

5.2 Garbage and recycling area: The enclosure at the south side of the building was clean and the lids on the dumpsters were closed. One (1) recycling bin had a cracked lid. The property manager stated that a replacement had been ordered.

5.3 Lighting: The light fixture above the west entrance door was not functioning at the time of inspection. The property manager stated that the bulb had burned out and would be replaced. All other exterior light fixtures observed were operational.

5.4 Mailroom: The mailroom door was unlocked during the inspection. The property manager stated that the door was kept unlocked during business hours and locked at all other times. The interior of the mailroom was clean and well lit. The floor was dry.

SECTION 6: MAINTENANCE AND FOLLOW-UP ITEMS

The following items were noted during the inspection. These items are not violations but are recorded for the property manager's reference and for follow-up by maintenance staff.

1. Unit 1B – Front door weather-stripping to be checked for draft.
2. Unit 2C – Hallway carpet near Apt. 2C to be checked for possible leaks; carpet staining noted.
3. Unit 3A – Bathroom ceiling condition; see Section 4. Tenant report of January 2024 to be verified.
4. Unit 3A – Bedroom window latch to be repaired or replaced.
5. Unit 3A – Bathroom exhaust fan noise to be checked.
6. Laundry room – Dryer vent hose to be reconnected at the wall connection; lint accumulation to be cleaned.
7. Common area – Handrail on east stairway to be tightened.
8. Common area – Recycling bin lid to be replaced.
9. Exterior – Light fixture above west entrance to be repaired.
10. Common hallways – Fire extinguisher inspection tags that were difficult to read to be replaced or re-issued.

---
The violation code listed for Item No. 1 (V-2341) is the current code for microbial growth and moisture intrusion, as of the date of this inspection. The property manager was provided with a copy of the code section and the associated guidance for remediation.

---

SECTION 7.1: DETAILED FINDINGS – ITEM NO. 1 (V-2341)

Unit 3A, Bathroom:

The bathroom ceiling and the upper portion of the wall above the bathtub show visible mold growth in an area approximately 2 feet by 3 feet. The surface is discolored (dark green/black) and appears to be active. The source of the moisture is likely the inoperable exhaust fan (Item No. 2) combined with the lack of a window in the bathroom. A moisture meter reading was taken at the ceiling surface; the reading was elevated at 28% (normal range for this surface is below 15%). The drywall at this location is soft to the touch and appears to be saturated.

The tenant of Unit 3A provided a written report dated January 2024 describing the condition. The property manager stated that a maintenance request was filed but that the work had not been scheduled due to a backlog of other requests. No prior inspection report for this unit was found in the department's files for the current ownership period.

A remediation plan will be required. The plan must include identification and repair of the moisture source, removal and replacement of affected drywall, and treatment of remaining surfaces for mold. The ventilation fan must be repaired or replaced as a separate item (Item No. 2). The property manager was advised that the tenant should be provided with alternate bathing facilities or the unit should be taken out of service if the condition worsens.

---

Unit 3A, Bathroom:

The exhaust fan did not operate when the wall switch was turned on. The fan housing was inspected; the motor was warm to the touch, indicating it may have been running continuously or recently. The property manager stated that the fan had "made noise for a while" and then stopped working. The fan is to be repaired or replaced. The duct to the exterior was not visible from the unit; the property manager stated that the duct runs through the attic and exits at the roof line. The condition of the duct was not verified during this inspection.

---

SECTION 7.3: DETAILED FINDINGS – ITEM NO. 3 (V-1154)

Unit 2C, Living Room:

A water stain approximately 12 inches in diameter is present on the ceiling near the window wall. The stain is brown in color and appears dry. No active leak was observed at the time of inspection. The unit above (Unit 3C) was not occupied at the time of inspection; the property manager stated that the unit had been vacant for two weeks and was being prepared for a new tenant. The source of the staining may be a previous leak from the vacant unit or from the roof. The property manager was instructed to have the source investigated and to document the findings. The ceiling surface did not appear to be sagging or soft.

---

SECTION 7.4: DETAILED FINDINGS – ITEM NO. 4 (V-1210)

Unit 1B, Kitchen:

The cabinet under the sink was wet on the interior. The floor under the cabinet was saturated. The property manager stated that the tenant had reported the leak on March 10, 2024, and that a work order had been created. A plumber had not yet been scheduled as of the inspection date. The shut-off valve for the sink was not accessible without removing stored items; the property manager was instructed to clear the area and to have the leak repaired as soon as possible. The floor covering is linoleum; the extent of any water damage to the subfloor is unknown at this time.

---

SECTION 7.5: DETAILED FINDINGS – ITEM NO. 5 (V-1099)

Common Area, East Stairway:

The handrail at the top post is loose. The post moves when pressure is applied to the rail. The fasteners at the base of the post were not visible; the post may be secured to the floor or to the wall. The property manager stated that the handrail had been noted in a previous inspection but that the repair had not been completed. This item is a repeat finding from the inspection of the property conducted on October 12, 2023. The handrail is to be repaired or replaced so that it is secure and does not move when used.

The violation code listed for Item No. 1 (V-2341) is the current code for microbial growth and moisture intrusion, as of the date of this inspection. The property manager was provided with a copy of the code section and the associated guidance for remediation.

SECTION 7.1: DETAILED FINDINGS – ITEM NO. 1 (V-2341)

Unit 3A, Bathroom:

The bathroom ceiling and the upper portion of the wall above the bathtub show visible mold growth in an area approximately 2 feet by 3 feet. The surface is discolored (dark green/black) and appears to be active. The source of the moisture is likely the inoperable exhaust fan (Item No. 2) combined with the lack of a window in the bathroom. A moisture meter reading was taken at the ceiling surface; the reading was elevated at 28% (normal range for this surface is below 15%). The drywall at this location is soft to the touch and appears to be saturated.

The tenant of Unit 3A provided a written report dated January 2024 describing the condition. The property manager stated that a maintenance request was filed but that the work had not been scheduled due to a backlog of other requests. No prior inspection report for this unit was found in the department's files for the current ownership period.

A remediation plan will be required. The plan must include identification and repair of the moisture source, removal and replacement of affected drywall, and treatment of remaining surfaces for mold. The ventilation fan must be repaired or replaced as a separate item (Item No. 2). The property manager was advised that the tenant should be provided with alternate bathing facilities or the unit should be taken out of service if the condition worsens.

---

Unit 3A, Bathroom:

The exhaust fan did not operate when the wall switch was turned on. The fan housing was inspected; the motor was warm to the touch, indicating it may have been running continuously or recently. The maintenance shop is a metal-clad building located in the northwest corner of the park.
The building was locked at the time of inspection. The property manager stated that the
shop contained tools, mowers, and bulk supplies. The exterior of the building was in good
condition. A small oil stain was noted on the concrete pad in front of the shop door; the
property manager stated that this was from a lawnmower and that it would be cleaned.

1.4 Trash Enclosures:

There are two trash enclosures, one near the clubhouse and one near the south entrance.
Both enclosures are constructed of wood fencing with gates. The gates were closed at the
time of inspection. Dumpsters were covered. No overflow of trash was observed. The
concrete pads under the dumpsters were clean.

SECTION 2: INTERNAL ROADS AND PARKING

2.1 Internal Roads:

All internal roads were paved. The pavement was in good condition with no significant
cracking or potholes. Speed bumps were painted and visible. Road signs, including stop
signs and speed limit signs, were present and legible.

2.2 Parking:

Each mobile home space has a designated parking area. The manager's office has three
visitor parking spaces. No vehicles were observed parked on grass or blocking internal
roads at the time of inspection.

SECTION 3: EXTERIOR OF INDIVIDUAL DWELLING UNITS

A walk-by exterior inspection was conducted of all 42 mobile home units. Units are
single-wide and double-wide manufactured homes on permanent foundations. Observations
were made from the public/common areas and from the internal roadways. No units were
entered.

3.1 General Exterior Conditions:

All units observed had intact siding, skirting, and roof coverings. No broken windows or
unsecured doors were noted. Several units had personal property (patio furniture, potted
plants, grills) on their porches or pads; these items were neatly arranged and did not
create a hazard or obstruct egress.

3.2 Skirting:

Skirting was present and intact on all units. A small gap (approx. 2 inches) was noted in
the skirting at the rear of Unit 27. The gap was not large enough to allow pest entry or
to constitute a code violation. Property manager was advised to monitor and repair if it
widens. This is a recommendation only.

PURPOSE OF RE-INSPECTION

This is a follow-up inspection to the initial inspection conducted on 03/12/2024 (Form 12-B, Report #2024-0312-SP). The purpose of this visit is to verify correction of the violations cited in the original report and to document any new conditions that may have arisen. The scope of this re-inspection is limited to the items listed in the original report, unless new violations are observed during the walk-through. The property manager accompanied the inspector for the duration of the inspection.

SUMMARY OF COMPLIANCE STATUS

Of the nine (9) violations cited in the original inspection report, eight (8) have been corrected and are in compliance. One (1) violation, the broken stair tread at Unit 14, has been partially corrected but does not meet the standard required by the Housing and Building Maintenance Code (HBMC). A new notice of violation will be issued for this item. No new violations were observed during this re-inspection. A complete item-by-item status is provided below.

ORIGINAL VIOLATION STATUS REPORT

Item 1 – Original Violation Code: 309.1 – Exterior stair tread broken, creating a trip hazard. Location: Unit 14, front porch stairs, second tread from the bottom.
Status: PARTIALLY CORRECTED – RE-VIOLATED

The second tread from the bottom on the front stairs of Unit 14 has been replaced. The replacement tread is pressure-treated lumber, which is an acceptable material. However, the tread is not securely fastened. The tread is only attached at the left stringer with a single screw. The right side of the tread is loose and moves vertically approximately 1/2 inch when pressure is applied. The gap between the tread and the stringer on the right side is approximately 1/4 inch. This condition creates a trip hazard and does not meet the requirement of the code, which requires that stairs be maintained in a safe and sound condition. The property manager stated that the repair was done by a handyman and that they would have it re-fastened. Inspector advised that the repair must be completed by a licensed contractor or a person with equivalent skill, and that all fasteners must be installed per manufacturer's specifications.

Item 2 – Original Violation Code: 307.1 – Damaged skirting at the rear of Unit 27. Gap approx. 2 inches, noted in initial inspection.
Status: CORRECTED

The gap in the skirting at the rear of Unit 27 has been repaired. The skirting panel has been re-secured and the gap is closed. The panel is flush with the adjacent panels and is properly fastened. No gap was observed at the time of this inspection. Compliance met.

Item 3 – Original Violation Code: 504.1 – Overflowing trash receptacle at the south entrance enclosure.
Status: CORRECTED

The dumpster at the south entrance enclosure was observed to be covered and not overflowing. The concrete pad under the dumpster was clean and free of debris. The gate to the enclosure was closed and latched. No trash was observed on the ground outside the enclosure. Compliance met.

Item 4 – Original Violation Code: 302.4 – Weeds and overgrown vegetation along the fence line at the north property boundary.
Status: CORRECTED

The vegetation along the north fence line has been cut and removed. The area is now clear of weeds and overgrowth. The fence line is visible and accessible. Compliance met.

Item 5 – Original Violation Code: 304.1 – Peeling paint on the exterior of Unit 5, south elevation.
Status: CORRECTED

The peeling paint on the south elevation of Unit 5 has been scraped and repainted. The new paint is applied evenly and appears to be a latex exterior paint. The surface is smooth and no peeling or flaking was observed. Compliance met.

area is now clear of weeds and overgrowth. The fence line is visible and
accessible. Compliance met.

of Unit 5, south elevation.

ceiling of the ground floor hallway, Building B.
Status: CORRECTED

The water-damaged ceiling section in the ground floor hallway of
Building B has been repaired. The damaged drywall was removed and
replaced, and the area has been painted. No stains, sagging, or
evidence of active leakage was observed. The repair appears sound.
Compliance met.

Item 8 – Original Violation Code: 307.1 – Loose handrail on the stairs
leading to the basement of Building A.
Status: CORRECTED

The handrail on the basement stairs of Building A is now secure. The
bracket at the top landing has been replaced and all fasteners are
tight. The handrail does not move when pressure is applied along its

manager stated the detector was installed on September 30, 2024.

repaired. The new siding matches the existing material and is
securely fastened. No gaps, holes, or warping were observed.
Compliance met.

securely anchored and meets the height requirement. The balusters are
spaced no more than 4 inches apart. Compliance met.

kitchen sink in Unit 4.

active leaks were observed. The cabinet floor shows no new water
damage. Compliance met.
